Description is blank; study 1 and p. 15 identify multiple outcomes and contrasts, without a row-specific test locator. No target assigned by row order, count of rows, or numeric matching. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
The 632 is the remaining participant pool across eight scenarios, not an established row-specific analytic N. Table 1 (printed p. 227/PDF p. 14) lists final scenario counts A=81, B=71, C=90, D=65, E=108, F=111, G=48, H=58, but excludes I-don’t-know responses from questions 1–13 and the printed test dfs vary by outcome. No N is inferred from df, no group sum is assigned, and no metric is converted. Note 20 gives explicit test-specific Ns only for its own chi-square tests; these remain candidates pending target identification. Exclusions are incomplete survey, incorrect response to either manipulation check, and prior college philosophy class. PDF pages 14–16 rendered and visually inspected.
Candidate evidence, not assigned to any audit row. PDF p. 15 = printed p. 228: mechanism main effects (note 13), universe main effects (note 14), interactions (note 15), Neuro/Psych Real t-tests (note 16), and Neuro/Psych Ertan t-tests (note 17). PDF p. 16 = printed p. 229: within-Neuro universe comparisons (note 18), within-Psych universe comparisons (note 19), and scenario-specific chi-square tests versus chance (note 20). Exact printed candidates:
All analyses were conducted on the remaining sample of 632
participants.

We excluded from analysis (and from results presented in Table 1) all participants
who did not complete the survey in full and all participants who responded incor-
rectly to either of the two manipulation checks (twenty-two percent of all partici-
pants).11 Since we are interested in pre-philosophical folk intuitions, we also
excluded those participants who indicated that they had taken a college philosophy
class (twenty-nine percent overall).

A 2 (mechanism: Psych, Neuro) ¥ 2 (universe: Real, Erta) Analysis of Vari-
ance (ANOVA) was run on the mean responses to our five primary variables of
interest (“up to,” FW, MR, blame, and praise; questions 1–5).12
